A probe with app env set to production got 419 on POST /api/posts, so real JSON API clients cannot create, update or delete posts. The suite only passes because CSRF is skipped while unit tests run.

v.rationale:
impl-2 and impl-3 are nearly the same in design: an enum cast, an observer that sets the slug and published_at, a policy enforced through middleware before validation, scopes, and a resource with plucked tag names. All three suites pass: impl-1 26 tests, impl-2 26, impl-3 19. My edge-case probes found no bugs in impl-2 or impl-3.

**1. impl-2:** Its tests are the most thorough: default page size, per_page bounds, and a guarantee that the slug stays stable. It uses typed request helpers ($request->integer) and selects only the needed tag columns. It has less ceremony than impl-3: no redundant 201, no global strict mode. Its one stylistic weakness is that it spells out the PUT/PATCH routes by hand.

**2. impl-3:** Clean apiResource routing and a sensible 'distinct' rule on tags. It loses ground for a redundant setStatusCode(201), HasMiddleware ceremony, an out-of-scope shouldBeStrict(), and a smaller test suite.

**3. impl-1:** Two real bugs, both confirmed by probes:
- It puts the 'web' middleware group on the API routes. With the env set to production, POST /api/posts returns 419 (CSRF), so API clients cannot write.
- It authorizes inside the controller after the FormRequest. A non-author with an invalid payload gets 422 instead of the required 403.
